column1: AI Lab: decision tree model
column5:
h3. Why
AI Lab has one machine learning algorithm: k-nearest neighbors. A student cannot compare two algorithms. A student also cannot read the model. A kd-tree is not legible. A shallow decision tree is legible, and a student can draw one by hand.

AI Lab also has no interface that lets you add a second algorithm. This epic adds the interface. It then adds the first algorithm that uses the interface.

h3. Terms
* A {{sweep}} is a search over candidate hyperparameter values. The trainer trains one model for each candidate, then keeps the most accurate model.
* A {{characterization test}} records the current behavior of the code, so that a later change cannot alter that behavior without a test failure.

h3. How this epic is split
* One ticket is one PR. Each ticket gives its branch and its merge order.
* Four tickets produce no PR: two decisions and two manual QA passes. Each of these tickets says so at the top of its description.
* Three tickets depend on nothing else in the epic. You can start them immediately: the App Lab hyperparameters reader, the {{ml-cart}} dependency, and the {{parseInt}} bug fix.
* Phases 1 to 3 are the first release. Phases 4 to 6 come after it: a student-set depth, removal of the legacy {{kValue}} write, and the tree visualization panel.

h3. Scope
* Lab2 only. Lab1 AI Lab uses a different copy of the machine learning code ({{@code-dot-org/ml-playground}}, in a different repository). That copy keeps KNN only.
* You do not need new localization strings.

h3. Writing convention
These tickets and the openspec documents use ASD-STE100. The specification files keep the RFC-2119 verb {{SHALL}}, because the openspec schema and the other openspec change in the repository use it.

h3. Reference
Full spec: {{openspec/changes/ailab-decision-tree/}} (proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, specs/)

column1: Retire the legacy kValue write
column5:
*Delivers:* one PR — {{ailab/retire-kvalue-write}}
*Merge order:* 18
*Blocked by:* Add the hyperparameters field to the saved model

h3. Why
A KNN model currently writes both `hyperparameters.k` and the top-level `kValue`. Once the reader has been deployed for a release, you can remove the duplicate write.

This ticket removes the WRITE only. The reader's fallback stays, permanently. Stored models stay in S3 forever. Every model saved before `hyperparameters` existed carries only `kValue`. App Lab projects refer to those models by id for years. If you remove the fallback read, a student's working project stops working.

h3. Scope
* Remove the `kValue` write from `getTrainedModelDataToSave`, and the field from `ModelDataToSave`.
* Leave the fallback read in `apps/src/MLTrainers.js`. Add a comment stating why it cannot be removed: stored models are permanent.
* Update the characterization test for the `kValue` field on a saved model.
* Out of scope: a backfill that rewrites stored models to add `hyperparameters`. A backfill would let you remove the fallback. It also rewrites student work in S3, and no user sees a result.

h3. Files
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/redux.ts}}
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/types.ts}}
* {{apps/src/MLTrainers.js (comment only)}}
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/test/unit/}}

h3. Acceptance criteria
* A newly saved KNN model carries `hyperparameters` and no `kValue`.
* A model saved before the field still predicts correctly in App Lab.
* The fallback read is still present, with a comment explaining why.

column1: Add ml-cart and its hand-written types

*Delivers:* one PR — {{ailab/add-ml-cart}}
*Merge order:* 10 (independent — you can start now)
*Blocked by:* nothing

h3. Why
`ml-cart` is the mljs CART implementation, from the same family as `ml-knn`. It ships no TypeScript types.

This lands as its own PR so the dependency and the hand-written types are reviewed and installed on their own. It depends on nothing. You can do it early, at the same time as other work.

h3. Scope
* Add `ml-cart` at the exact version 2.1.1 to `frontend/packages/labs/ailab/package.json` and to `apps/package.json`.
* Use the exact version, not a caret range. This departs from the neighboring `ml-knn` entries, which both use `^3.0.0`. The types are hand-written here, and a minor bump can silently invalidate them.
* Add an `ml-cart` declaration block to `src/declarations.d.ts`, patterned on the existing `ml-knn` block. Declare `DecisionTreeClassifier` and `DecisionTreeRegression`, each with `train`, `predict`, `toJSON` and a static `load`.
* Type `predict` as taking `number[][]` and returning `number[]`. A flat array throws at runtime, so the type must not allow one.

h3. Files

* {{apps/package.json}}
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/declarations.d.ts}}

h3. Acceptance criteria
* `typecheck` passes with the new types.
* The declared options are `gainFunction`, `splitFunction`, `minNumSamples`, `maxDepth` and `gainThreshold`.
* The lock file updates in the same PR.

column1: Implement DecisionTreeTrainer with a maxDepth sweep
column5:
*Delivers:* one PR — {{ailab/decision-tree-trainer}}
*Merge order:* 11
*Blocked by:* Add ml-cart and its hand-written types; Remove the Redux round-trip from the k sweep

h3. Why
This is the feature. A student can read a shallow decision tree. A student cannot read a kd-tree.

This PR includes the tests. Do not put them in a later PR. A reviewer cannot approve a trainer that has no tests.

h3. Scope
* Add `src/trainers/DecisionTreeTrainer.ts` implementing `Trainer`.
* Pick `DecisionTreeClassifier` or `DecisionTreeRegression` from `isRegression(state)`.
* Sweep `maxDepth` over [1, 2, 3, 5, 8]. Grade each tree with `gradeAccuracy`, and keep the most accurate.
* On equal accuracy keep the LOWER depth. This differs from the `k` sweep, which keeps the first highest scorer. A shallow tree is the reason to offer a tree at all.
* Pass `minNumSamples: 1`, not the library default of 3. Measured on a 9-row training set, the default misclassifies training rows that 1 classifies correctly. AI Lab datasets are small. A large minimum leaf size makes a tree that has only one leaf.
* Record `{maxDepth, minNumSamples}` in `hyperparameters`. Write no `kValue`.
* Register the trainer under the `decisionTree` family, mapping to `treeClassify` and `treeRegress` by label column type.
* Test the full flow with the `train.test.js` pattern.
* Test the tie-break: equal accuracy at two depths stores the shallower tree.
* Test that a regression prediction can fall between observed label values.
* Test the JSON round-trip for both tree kinds.

h3. Files
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/trainers/DecisionTreeTrainer.ts (new)}}
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/trainers/ (registry)}}
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/test/unit/}}

h3. Acceptance criteria
* Two depths with equal accuracy store the shallower tree.
* A regression prediction is asserted to be a value present in no training label.
* The round-trip test asserts identical predictions before and after serialization.
* The trainer is unreachable from any level until the next ticket lands. That is expected.

column1: Fix the parseInt truncation in convertTestValue
column5:
*Delivers:* one PR — {{ailab/fix-parseint-truncation}}
*Merge order:* 14 (independent — you can start now)
*Blocked by:* nothing

h3. Why
`convertTestValue` in `apps/src/MLTrainers.js` ends with `parseInt(convertedValue)`. The lab trains on the result of `parseFloat`. So every continuous feature value is truncated at prediction time: a temperature of 72.8 trains as 72.8 and predicts as 72.

This is a live defect in KNN prediction today, not a decision tree problem. It depends on nothing in this epic and can ship at any point. A tree makes the result worse. If a threshold is between two integers, the truncated value goes down the other branch.

h3. Scope
* Change `parseInt` to `parseFloat`.
* A categorical value still resolves through `featureNumberKey` first, so its integer is unaffected.
* Call the fix out in the PR description. It changes prediction results on existing levels.

h3. Files
* {{apps/src/MLTrainers.js}}

h3. Acceptance criteria
* A feature value of 72.8 reaches the model as 72.8.
* A categorical feature value still resolves to its integer.
* Tests cover both cases.

column1: Let a student choose the tree depth
column5:
*Delivers:* one PR — {{ailab/student-depth-control}}
*Merge order:* 17
*Blocked by:* Accept an externally set tree depth

h3. Why
Depth is the control that teaches the lesson. A student who moves it and watches accuracy change sees overfitting happen. The sweep prevents this, because it selects the depth for the student.

h3. Scope
* Agree three points with curriculum before you build. The design records them as an open question.
* Point 1: where the control sits in the flow.
* Point 2: the range of depths a student can choose.
* Point 3: whether accuracy updates on each change, or only on an explicit retrain.
* Add a `mode` opt-in, so only levels that ask for the control show it.
* Add the control to the train step, and retrain on change.
* Record the depth in `hyperparameters` with source `student`.
* Keep the sweep as the default for every level that does not opt in.

h3. Files
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/types.ts}}
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/UIComponents/TrainModel.tsx}}
* {{frontend/packages/labs/ailab/src/redux.ts}}

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Changing the depth retrains, and the reported accuracy moves.

* Flag a tie leaf, such as `[[0, 0.5, 0.5]]`. The library resolves it to the first class; a view may want to say so.

column1: Decide what the tree panel shows and where it lives
column5:
*Delivers:* no PR
*Blocked by:* Implement DecisionTreeTrainer with a maxDepth sweep

h3. Why
No PR. A design and curriculum decision that gates the panel.

The lab shows no model structure for any algorithm today, so there is no precedent to follow. Two measured facts about ml-cart 2.1.1 constrain the answer.

First, a leaf carries no sample count. Only internal nodes have `numberSamples`. A leaf has a proportional `distribution` such as `[[0, 0.5, 0.5]]`, so "18 of 25 examples" is not available from the model. To show counts, the lab must send the training rows down the tree. This is extra work, and it is a separate decision.

Second, CART splits an ordinal-encoded categorical feature on a numeric threshold. A split renders as `shape < 1.5`, which means nothing to a student. The panel needs a rule for a categorical split, or the levels need to avoid categorical features.

h3. Scope
* Decide: its own panel in the flow, or a section of the existing results or model summary panel.
* Decide what a node shows: feature, threshold, gain, sample count, class mix.
* Decide the rule for rendering a categorical split.
* Decide the behavior for a tree too large to draw, and whether depth is capped for readability.
* Decide whether leaf sample counts justify recomputing them from the training rows.
